Print a topic model

Source: R/topics.R
print.sbert_topic_model.Rd

print() shows a fitted topic model at a glance: the number of documents (and of segments, for a segmented fit), the number of topics, the embedding model, the clustering algorithm, the size of every topic, and the share of the embedding variance that lies between topics.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sbert_topic_model'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A topic model fitted by topics().

...

Ignored.

Value

x, invisibly.

See also

summary() for coherence and topic diversity; topic_sizes() for the labeled size table; as.data.frame() for the tables.

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
print(topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
             embeddings = feedback_embeddings))
#> <sbert_topic_model>
#>   documents: 600 
#>   topics: 6
#>   model: precomputed embeddings
#>   algorithm: deterministic k-means (Lloyd)
#>   topic sizes: 223, 133, 131, 49, 37, 27
#>   between/total SS: 22.6%
